blockers.summary: Reviewer requests changes: "…The description seems a bit unfinished, please update…" (obondarev)

The change is a new feature (an approved RFE) backported to stable/2024.1 and stable/2024.2. SRU policy normally rejects feature backports, and no SRU justification, regression analysis or test plan is given.

The fix depends on ovsdbapp Address_Set support (ovsdbapp review 905044). The yoga backport was abandoned over this dependency. The ovsdbapp and OVN versions packaged in the target Ubuntu series may not have it, so the neutron backport could break or do nothing there.

Both stable backports were cherry-picked with conflicts in the functional test file and the release note. The tempest-plugin job that exercises the feature merged only on master, after the backports. The backported code may therefore be untested on the stable branches.

The RFE was approved on the condition of no API or DB changes. The change affects how ACLs are generated for existing ML2/OVN deployments, and no upgrade or migration handling is described. Existing deployments may get different ACLs or Address_Set entries after the update.

comments.body:
Hi Dean,

In d/p/lp2085314-fix-stack-overflow-when-dropping-tclass-qdisc.patch,
the "Forwarded" and "Signed-off-by": tags are unnecessary. 

Additionally, the Origin tag:

Origin: upstream, https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/32258/changes/632d321050f58fe1b5bed7cfe769d212377c0301

should really point to the commit that landed in the main branch, and not what
is in the pull request, such as:

Origin: upstream, https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/632d321050f58fe1b5bed7cfe769d212377c0301

The "Bug-Ubuntu" tag could also be minified to:

Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/2085314

You could have also included the upstream bug with:

Bug: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/32247

The same applies to d/p/lp2085314-avoid-concurrent-set-modification-tclass-qdisc.patch.

Now, in your merge requests, it is also a good idea to try suggest a suitable
version for your changelog entries. I know this will managed by Nick in systemd,
but not all packages are carefully taken care of by an engineering team, and it
is best to put forward versions that are suitable. 

You can learn more about versions in this page here:

https://ubuntu.com/project/docs/how-ubuntu-is-made/concepts/version-strings/#version-adding-a-change-in-ubuntu-as-a-stable-release-update

Nick has accepted your patches as they are, and they are okay, you don't need to
edit them, this is more of a heads up for next time.

Well done on landing patches into systemd for one of your first SRUs.

Thanks,
Matthew

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…to 64. This could produce a performance regression for some users, as the performance bottleneck of this cap was significant enoug…" (whershberger)

The backported patches parse /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, so the default value is always used and the system limit is never honored. The fix is not merged upstream, and the SRU does not yet include it.

The fallback value from get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX, which effectively disables the cap. A conservative default (65530) is needed, and the upstream patch is not yet merged or included in the SRU.

The fix reads /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count, which needs a libvirt AppArmor profile change (LP #2170732). QEMU also needs a versioned Breaks on libvirt, otherwise guests could fail or the profile could deny the read after upgrade. Neither is confirmed done.

The fix only reduces the risk and does not remove it. Crashes are still possible with many vCPUs or IOThreads, and a reproducer crashed at 255 vCPUs under the Noble limit. The reproducer for the patched package has only been shown to lower the VMA peak, not to stay below the limit.

Reviewer asked whether QEMU still crashes when the limit is hit with the fix applied. The answer was that a smaller chance of a crash remains. Behavior at the limit is not fully characterized, including migration-thread contributions.

The impact analysis kept changing (vCPU thread-local caches, a test plan with CPU overcommit, and a reproducer needing a pc-i440fx machine with IDE cdrom). The SRU justification and test plan may need to be re-validated against the final package. Live-migration scenarios were not explored.
